title: Supported coherent first-page CE lifts
statement: For each scheme X [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and bounded-below complex K of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], simultaneously choose presentations D(X,K) [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation], sequence maps M for inverse-image chain maps v:f^{-1}K -> L [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and actual cycle/boundary quotient realizations e [lem-weil-pbc-ce-stationary-page-naturality]. The first-page equation is cohomology pullback followed by Sheaf.H.map(v.f q) [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Each v admits a strictly augmented CE total lift u; its sections-total map [lem-weil-pbc-ce-total-sections-comparison] preserves every filtration step and induces M on graded cycle representatives as in EtaleCEPageMapOnRepresentatives. In addition, for every lower support bound a of K and every degree n, the degree-n filtration step at a is top and that at n+1 is bottom. No stationary page comparison, homology-step maps, or naturality on the abutment is asserted.

proof.text: Construct raw augmented CE resolutions preserving every lower support bound, using intrinsic zero-object choices in the two horseshoe rows. Choose these existential witnesses simultaneously. Each input complex has a lower bound by membership in CochainComplex.Plus, so the chosen raw resolutions are bounded below.

Construct coherent first pages and strictly augmented filtered lifts on precisely these prescribed raw resolutions. Keep the supplied bicomplex through the equality D.I=I, retaining the first-page and representative equations.

For each input support bound b, extend the resolution degree by zero and flip after global sections. Negative resolution summands are zero by extension; complex degrees below b are zero by the raw support condition and preservation of zero objects. Apply boundedBelow_secondFiltration. The two filtration formulas identify its degreewise steps with D.L, proving top at b and bottom at n+1. This also applies to the all-zero complex and degrees below b.
